```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

## 1. Significance of Predictors in Multiple Linear Regression

```{r}
# Simulated coefficients and p-values
coefficients <- data.frame(
  Predictor = c("TV", "Radio", "Newspaper"),
  Coefficient = c(0.0475, 0.179, -0.001),
  P_Value = c(0.00001, 0.00001, 0.86)
)
coefficients
```

## 2. Predicting Salary Using Interaction Terms

```{r}
beta_0 <- 50; beta_1 <- 20; beta_2 <- 0.07
beta_3 <- 35; beta_4 <- 0.01; beta_5 <- -10

GPA <- 4.0; IQ <- 110; Level <- 1
predicted_salary <- beta_0 + beta_1 * GPA + beta_2 * IQ + beta_3 * Level +
  beta_4 * GPA * IQ + beta_5 * GPA * Level
predicted_salary
```

## 3. Simple Linear Regression: Passes Through the Mean

```{r}
set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(100)
y <- 3 + 2 * x + rnorm(100)
model <- lm(y ~ x)

mean_x <- mean(x)
mean_y <- mean(y)
predict(model, data.frame(x = mean_x))
```

## 4. Modeling mpg with Horsepower in Auto Dataset

```{r}
auto_data <- read.table("Auto.data", header=TRUE, na.strings="?")
auto_data <- na.omit(auto_data)

model <- lm(mpg ~ horsepower, data = auto_data)
summary(model)
```

## 5. Confidence and Prediction Intervals

```{r}
predict(model, data.frame(horsepower = 98), interval = "confidence")
predict(model, data.frame(horsepower = 98), interval = "prediction")
```

## 6. Diagnostic Plots

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)
```

## 7. No-Intercept Linear Regression

```{r}
set.seed(1)
x <- rnorm(100)
y <- 2 * x + rnorm(100)
lm(y ~ x + 0)
```

## 8. Multicollinearity Simulation

```{r}
set.seed(1)
x1 <- runif(100)
x2 <- 0.5 * x1 + rnorm(100) / 10
y <- 2 + 2 * x1 + 0.3 * x2 + rnorm(100)

model <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2)
summary(model)
cor(x1, x2)
```

## 9. High-Leverage Point

```{r}
x1 <- c(x1, 0.1); x2 <- c(x2, 0.8); y <- c(y, 6)
model <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2)
summary(model)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)
```
